about: Why we forget a name so quickly

lines.text: Most of us have met someone at a party and forgotten the name within seconds.
Scientists say this is not a sign for a poor memory. A name, unlike
lines.note: Preposition: it is 'a sign of' something.

lines.text: a job or a hobby, tells us nothing about the person, although the brain
lines.note: Connector: having little to attach the name to is a result, so it is 'so'.

say next, which leaves little attend for the introduction itself. Researchers have

lines.text: found that people who repeat a name aloud remembered it far more often.
lines.note: Tense: this is a general fact, so it is 'remember'.

lines.text: Linking the name with something familiar is also helpful. If you meet a
Mr Baker, you might picture him hold a loaf of bread. Such images,
